result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked zebra crosswalks, sidewalks, and curb ramps within a residential context. However, the environment lacks dedicated pedestrian signals and traffic-calming features like street trees or curb extensions, which may lead to higher vehicle speeds and increased exposure.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated walk/don't-walk signals are visible at this signalized intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle signal timing.
hazards.location_in_image: At the signalized corner poles

hazards.name: Wide Curb Radii
hazards.description: The corner geometry appears wide, which can encourage higher vehicle turning speeds through the crosswalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Corner of the intersection in the foreground

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and slow down turning vehicles by tightening the corner radius.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees along the sidewalk to provide a vertical buffer between pedestrians and traffic while naturally calming vehicle speeds.

result.summary: The intersection features basic pedestrian infrastructure including marked continental crosswalks, pedestrian signals, and curb ramps. However, safety is compromised by visual obstructions from parked vehicles and large corner vegetation, as well as a lack of physical traffic calming measures like curb extensions or refuge islands.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection obscure the sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb on the right side of the main roadway

hazards.name: Vegetation Obstruction
hazards.description: A large tree on the corner may partially block the view of pedestrian signals or approaching traffic for people on the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Far left corner of the intersection

hazards.name: Road Surface Debris
hazards.description: Loose dirt or debris is visible within the crosswalk area, which can affect traction or indicate poor maintenance.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the intersection within the crosswalk markings

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Maintenance
interventions.description: Repave the intersection and refresh markings to ensure a smooth, high-contrast crossing surface.

result.summary: The intersection is currently a construction zone with significant dirt and debris obscuring pavement markings and sidewalk paths. While traffic lights are present, the lack of clear pedestrian signals and the presence of heavy machinery near the crossing create a hazardous environment for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Construction Debris
hazards.description: Dirt and sand cover the roadway and sidewalk areas, obscuring markings and creating a slip hazard.
hazards.location_in_image: Intersection corners and roadway surface

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Equipment
hazards.description: A backhoe and trailer are parked near the intersection, blocking sightlines between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Left side of the intersection near the sidewalk

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalks
hazards.description: The crosswalk markings are faded and partially covered by dirt, reducing their visibility to drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Repaint crosswalks with high-visibility continental markings once construction is complete.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signals with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten crossing distances and improve the visibility of pedestrians waiting to cross.

result.summary: The image shows a residential intersection with marked continental crosswalks and overhead traffic signals. While sidewalks and basic crossing markings are present, the wide roadway and lack of visible pedestrian-specific signals or refuge islands increase exposure for those crossing.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide roadway requires pedestrians to be exposed to traffic for an extended period without a refuge island.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the marked crosswalk.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb may obscure pedestrians, especially children, from the view of approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the right side of the roadway near the intersection.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking within 20 feet of the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised island in the center of the roadway to allow for two-stage crossing.
